title: The author names the archetype for the new service
STEGO writes the declaration with the archetype's smallest example content, and a folder for fills
An archetype the registry does not hold is refused, with the archetypes it does hold
A declaration already present stops the scaffold, and no file changes
Asked for an empty scaffold, STEGO leaves the example content out and names every setting the author must supply
The agent names the archetype it writes for
STEGO reports the active component set's components, each setting with its type and allowed values, and each slot, as structured data
The author asks STEGO to check the declaration, and STEGO reports every fault or that there is none
A declaration that holds an acceptance past its date is refused, naming the component and the date
The agent reads each fault: the rule it breaks, its path, what was found and what is allowed
The agent changes the declaration at the path each fault names
The agent asks STEGO to check the declaration again
The platform engineer names the component digest and the checkouts to search
STEGO reads the committed record in each checkout, and names each service that pins the digest, with its version and digest
A checkout with generated output and no readable record is reported as unknown
The platform engineer changes one component, and the registry publishes its new digest
The platform engineer records the new digest as the successor of the old one, with the fail date and whether taking it needs a declaration or fill change
A consumer moves that component's pin alone and runs apply in Generating, and keeps its compiler pin
A supersession with no successor, no fail date or no statement of the change it needs is refused
The service author runs validate or plan
STEGO reports each superseded pin with its successor and fail date, and does not fail for that reason
Past its fail date, validate fails for the pin
Past its fail date, apply in Generating refuses to write
When STEGO cannot read the lifecycle records, it reports that it could not check, and does not report the pins as current
The platform engineer asks STEGO for every recorded service that pins the digest
The platform engineer records the withdrawal, with the future date after which the digest fails
After the date, validate fails for every service that still pins the digest
A withdrawal whose date is already past is refused
Apply in Generating refuses a new pin to a withdrawn digest at once, whatever the date of the withdrawal
The platform engineer names the commit to qualify
STEGO finds the checks run and the signed artifact run at exactly that commit, and requires a success conclusion for every required job
STEGO installs the published release through the consumer path, and cross-checks each asset digest against the qualified artifacts
A run from another commit, or a required job with no success conclusion, fails qualification
A release tag that points at another commit fails verification
The operator names the release by its full source commit
The installer checks each asset digest and both signatures, and the signed record's platform, then puts the binary and its build record in place
The operator asks the installed compiler for its build identity, and it reports the identity it writes into a service's record
On any platform other than Linux amd64, the installer refuses before it downloads anything
The service author runs apply, and STEGO writes the generated files and the record together
The service author commits the record with the generated code
An interrupted apply leaves a journal, and plan, apply and drift refuse until the author runs recover
The platform engineer asks STEGO to check the record, and STEGO names every generated file that no longer matches its hash
A record that disagrees with itself, or that names a registry or compiler its state does not hold, is reported as broken
The service author moves the component's pin to the successor digest
The service author runs plan, and STEGO saves the plan and lists each file that the new digest changes
The service author runs apply, and STEGO changes only the files that the new digest affects
The service author reads the diff of the fix and commits it with the record
Apply names every generated file that no longer matches its hash, and writes nothing
When the author states on the command that the run may replace hand-edited files, apply replaces them
STEGO reports the standing of each pin, the successor included, and the author goes on only when no pin is withdrawn or past its fail date
A pin that is withdrawn or past its fail date stops the author before apply, and the author moves it to a digest that stands
The service author changes the declaration
STEGO reports the standing of each pin before the change is applied, and the author goes on only when no pin is withdrawn or past its fail date
The service author runs apply, and STEGO plans in the same run and writes the changed files, deletes the files it no longer generates, and writes the record
The service author reads the diff of the declaration change and commits it with the declaration and the record
A failed validation, generator or assembly stops the run, STEGO names the failure, and no file changes
The service author runs plan, and STEGO saves the plan and lists each change
The service author reads the saved plan
The service author runs apply with the saved plan, and STEGO writes exactly what it names
An input, the record or a generated file changed after planning, so apply refuses the plan and the author plans again
Plan, apply and drift refuse while a journal is pending, and name recover
The service author runs recover, and STEGO completes the journal
A journaled file matches neither of its states, so recover names it and changes nothing
The platform engineer defines each port the component provides that the registry does not hold yet
The platform engineer declares each slot the component offers, with its protobuf contract
The platform engineer adds the component with its config schema, its ports, its slots and its namespace, and STEGO accepts it before its generator runs
The platform engineer states each thing the emitted code must always do as an output contract, with the generator that builds it and the test that proves it
The platform engineer changes what the generator emits, and releases the component at a new version
A namespace that another component of the registry claims is refused, naming both components
The platform engineer pins the common registry at one reference
The platform engineer names a local registry that adds the team's own parts, at one reference
STEGO composes the sources into one active set, and records the reference of each
A local part that would replace a common part is refused, naming the part and both registries
The platform engineer chooses the components the archetype includes, and the component that answers each port by default
STEGO accepts the archetype with its smallest example content, which a fresh declaration of it passes checking with
A required port with no provider, or with more than one, is refused, naming the port and every component involved
A component that is not ga is refused, naming the component and its stage
A mixin that brings a component that is not ga is refused, naming the component and its stage
The platform engineer gives the component a port name of its own, which no ga component provides
The platform engineer adds the component at stage alpha, with the date it stops working
A service that wants the component accepts it by name in its declaration, with a date of its own
A sunset date that is already past is refused
The platform engineer reads every recorded service that uses the component
The platform engineer moves the component up to ga, which removes its sunset date and lets it take over the real port name
The platform engineer withdraws a component that will not graduate
STEGO reports every service that still uses a component past its sunset, and checking fails for each of them
